correctness.rationale: For all fixed coprime p/q and complementary distinct frequencies, first-order forcing vanishes by roots-of-unity orthogonality. At order two, exact Fourier summation leaves only 0 and ±q and yields a nonvanishing q-mode Cq=(π q AB/4)[-(n-m)cot(πpm/q)+iq] exp(i(φ+ψ)). The implicit return condition and monotonicity in ω prove the endpoints. For odd q, signed-pair resonance at ±q occurs exactly when m+n=q; otherwise the return coefficient is spatially constant. A self-contained checker passes 306 tests; finite tests alone are not proof.

value.rationale: The measured mathematical invariant is the small-forcing width of a natural rational mode-locking region. For the 2022 physical two-harmonic map its first nontrivial 1/3 coefficient is explicit, and for arbitrary denominators the result reveals a selection rule: the matching sum of just two harmonics can generate an order-ε² tongue even at large q. The odd-q converse is a complete and phase-robust onset classification. The result is more than a software test or arbitrary parameter slice; it answers how coupling harmonic content changes synchronization robustness.
